name: Lakshmi Devi
headline: 71-year-old water quality monitor in Karnataka
title: The University Van is About to Leave
situation: Lakshmi is at the river bend collecting a sample from a shallow well when she hears the university van honk twice from the main road—the agreed signal that they are leaving in ten minutes. As she straightens up, she notices a woman she does not recognize drawing water for her children from a nearby hand pump that Lakshmi has not tested this month. The woman smiles and offers her a drink. Lakshmi can either walk quickly to the van without explaining, or take five minutes to test the pump with her arsenic strip and risk making the driver wait.

context.relationship_profiles: Lakshmi has a cordial but punctuality-sensitive relationship with the van driver, who once threatened to leave without her when she was ten minutes late. The unknown woman is a young mother from a neighboring hamlet; Lakshmi has seen her drawing water here before but never spoken.
context.tendencies: When she sees a hand pump used by children, she has often interrupted her route to test it, even if it meant arriving late to the lab. She has also, on occasion, skipped a test to keep the van driver from honking again, because she values his help.
context.current_state: She has just walked six kilometres carrying a bucket of samples and feels a familiar ache in her knees, but she is still steady on her feet. Her mind is calm, focused on the task; she is not yet tired enough to hurry without reason.
context.immediate_memories: The woman’s smile and the offer of water remind her of her own daughter as a child, who once drank from a pump that later tested positive for arsenic. The honk of the van recalls a previous occasion when the driver left without her, forcing her to walk twelve kilometres back to the village.
context.reflective_memories: She remembers the many times she tested a pump that others had dismissed, and found it unsafe, saving children from sickness. She also recalls that the university students rely on her samples being on time for their afternoon experiments.
